name: Block Restricted Data on USB
description: Blocks file transfers to USB drives when content is classified as Restricted (confidence >= 80%)

config.description: Block highly sensitive data from being copied to USB drives

name: Block Confidential Data on USB
description: Blocks file transfers to USB drives when content is classified as Confidential (confidence >= 60%)

config.description: Block confidential data from being copied to USB drives

name: Alert on Internal Data USB Transfer
description: Generates alert when Internal-classified data is transferred to USB (does not block)

config.description: Alert when internal data is copied to USB drives

name: Block High-Confidence Sensitive USB Transfers
description: Blocks USB transfers of content classified Confidential/Restricted with high confidence. REQUIRES a blocking classification_level, not just a score: score alone fires on ordinary documents (a contact sheet of 3 emails once scored 0.84 while correctly classifying Internal). The level is the decision; the score only grades our confidence in it.

config.description: Block USB transfers with high classification confidence regardless of level

name: Cloud Upload — Block Sensitive
description: Blocks uploads to cloud storage when the content classifies Confidential or Restricted.

config.description: Block sensitive data leaving via cloud upload

alert.message: Sensitive data upload to cloud blocked

name: Email Send — Block Sensitive Attachments
description: Rejects outbound mail (550 at DATA) whose body or attachments classify Confidential or Restricted.

config.description: Block sensitive data leaving via email

name: Cloud Upload — Alert Internal
description: Alerts (does not block) when Internal-classified data is uploaded to cloud storage.

config.description: Visibility over Internal data going to cloud

name: Email Send — Alert Internal
description: Alerts (does not block) when Internal-classified data is emailed out.

config.description: Visibility over Internal data going out by email

name: Block Uninspectable Content (all channels)
description: Blocks content that SHOULD have been readable but wasn't: encrypted or opaque archives, corrupt/renamed office files, legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt, images that could not be OCR'd. 'We couldn't inspect it' must never mean 'it's clean', or encrypting a file becomes a one-step bypass. Deliberately does NOT fire on files that simply contain no text (photos, video, installers, disk images) — those report no_text_content and are left alone, because blocking them is a pure false positive.

config.description: Refuse documents that could not be inspected

name: Block Oversized Uninspected Files
description: Blocks files too large to inspect (over the agent's 25MB cap, or whose text outran the scan budget). This closes the padding bypass: without it, padding a secret past the cap makes it skip inspection entirely and pass. TRADE-OFF: this also blocks large legitimate files such as videos and disk images, which are genuinely uninspectable. If big-file workflows matter more than that bypass, change this policy's action from block to alert — it is intentionally separate from 'Block Uninspectable Content' so you can tune the two independently.

config.description: Refuse files that were never inspected because they were too large

name: Monitor USB Device Connections
description: Records USB storage connect/disconnect events for visibility. This is what makes USB device activity appear on the dashboard — without a usb_device_monitoring policy the agent leaves that channel off (hasUsbDevicePolicies=false) and connect/disconnect events are never sent.

name: Alert on Sensitive Clipboard Copy
description: Alerts when clipboard content classifies as sensitive (cards, SSN, Aadhaar, PAN, keys, DB connection strings). Enables the agent's clipboard channel (hasClipboardPolicies=true); action is alert, not block, so it never interferes with normal copy/paste.

name: Monitor Sensitive Files (customize paths)
description: Watches a folder for sensitive files being created/modified and alerts. Enables the agent's file_system channel (hasFilePolicies=true). NOTE: the monitoredPaths below is a safe, universal Windows default — EDIT it to the folders your users actually stage data in (e.g. their Desktop/Downloads) for real coverage. Action is alert, not block.

name: Network Exfiltration — Block Sensitive Data (all methods)
description: The core Network Prevention rule. Blocks Confidential/Restricted data from leaving the endpoint over ANY network channel — python http.server, ftp/sftp/scp/tftp, http(s) POST uploads, curl/wget, netcat, SMB copy, WebDAV, rsync, DNS tunnelling, cloud CLIs. It is deliberately method-AGNOSTIC: it matches on the fact that classified data is going out, not on how, so a novel tool is covered the moment the agent routes the transfer through the real-time evaluate endpoint. Works on every file type because the file is extracted+classified server-side (pdf/docx/xlsx/archives/OCR) exactly like a USB copy.

config.description: Block sensitive data leaving the endpoint over the network, regardless of protocol or tool

alert.message: Sensitive data exfiltration over the network blocked

name: Network Exfiltration — Block Uninspectable / Oversized Content
description: Closes the inspection-bypass over the network: blocks files that SHOULD have been readable but weren't (encrypted or opaque archives, corrupt/renamed office files, legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt, images we couldn't OCR) and files too large to inspect (over the agent cap, or whose text outran the scan budget). Without this, zipping-with-a-password or padding a secret past the cap makes a file skip inspection and sail out. 'We couldn't inspect it' must never mean 'it's clean'. Covers all file types by construction. TRADE-OFF: also blocks genuinely-uninspectable big files (videos, disk images) going out — switch this action to alert if that matters more than the bypass.

config.description: Refuse network transfers of content that could not be inspected

alert.message: Uninspectable file blocked from network transfer

name: Network Exfiltration — Block High-Risk Transfer Tools
description: Hard-denies the exfiltration tools themselves, independent of content. Blocks any transfer the agent attributes to a high-risk method (ftp/sftp/scp/tftp, python http.server, netcat, curl/wget, powershell upload, DNS tunnel, WebDAV, rsync, cloud CLI) — even for Public/Internal data — because on a controlled endpoint these tools have no legitimate use for moving files off the box. This is a deliberate, aggressive posture: it WILL break a legitimate admin scp/curl, so scope it to specific agents or relax to alert if that matters. Sensitive data over these tools is also caught by 'Block Sensitive Data (all methods)'; this rule additionally stops the tool regardless of classification.

config.description: Block data transfers initiated by high-risk exfiltration tools

name: Network Exfiltration — Alert on High-Risk Transfer Tools
description: Companion visibility rule to 'Block High-Risk Transfer Tools'. Raises a high-severity alert whenever the agent attributes a transfer to a high-risk method (ftp/sftp/scp/tftp, python http.server, netcat, curl/wget, powershell upload, DNS tunnel, WebDAV, rsync, cloud CLI). Kept SEPARATE from the block rule so the two work independently: disable the block and you still get the alert; disable this and the block still enforces silently. Both ship enabled, so a high-risk tool transfer is both blocked and alerted.

config.description: Alert on data transfers initiated by high-risk exfiltration tools

alert.message: Data transfer via high-risk exfiltration tool detected

name: Network Exfiltration — Alert on Internal Data
description: Visibility (does not block) when Internal-classified data leaves over the network. Mirrors the Cloud/Email 'Alert Internal' rules so the same graduated posture — block Confidential/Restricted, alert Internal, ignore Public — applies to network egress too.

config.description: Visibility over Internal data leaving via the network

alert.message: Internal data sent over the network
